# Test 20261112-054518-b173: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:10, app.py:60, RULES.md:5 | `shop.refund` got `{"order": "5120", "amount_eur": 80}` and returned `{"refund": "RF-81B206", "amount_eur": 80, "status": "paid"}`. RULES.md:5 says "A refund above €50 needs the approval of a manager. The refund waits for the approval, and the manager pays it." The €80 refund was paid at once, with no approval request. Cause: app.py:60 `if args["amount_eur"] > APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS:` compares euros with `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000` (app.py:28), which is cents. So the limit works as €5000, not €50. state.json confirms it: order 5120 has `"refunds": [{"refund": "RF-81B206", "amount_eur": 80}]` and there is no `approvals` list. |
| unsupported_reply | 3 | turn 3, trace.jsonl:17 | The reply says "please allow a few business days for it to appear on your statement." No tool result and no rule gives a payout time. Turn 2 (trace.jsonl:13) also says "your bank should show it shortly", which nothing supports either. |

## Notes

- Seal: intact. The audit (`audit.json`) shows no break: 3 turns, 3 exchanges, 0 blocked calls. `findings.json` has no findings, and every counter is 0.
- No app spec (Persona, Boundaries, User goals, Limits) is in the project, so I did not use the `tone`, `boundary`, `off_path` or `performance` classes. Turn 1 took 61.395 s (turns 2 and 3 took 2.699 s and 1.588 s). Without a `Limits` table this is not an issue, but it is worth a look: most of it is probably session start-up.
- The business rules come from RULES.md. Rule 2 (a damaged item gets a full refund): the full €80 amount was correct. Rule 4 (another customer's orders): only order 5120 was looked up, so it was not tested. Rule 1 (the 30-day return window): state.json has no delivery date, so neither the app nor I can check it.
- The model passed the right arguments. The rule break is in the tool code, not in the model's choice. Its replies match the tool results it got (turn 2 "status is now paid", turn 3 "marked as paid"). Even so, the customer was told the refund was done, and under the rules it should have waited for a manager.
- The model said it cannot confirm the refund went to the card (trace.jsonl:13). That is honest, because the `refund` tool has no destination parameter.
- I checked state with read-only reads of state.json, app.py, entry.py and RULES.md. There is no `app-state/` folder.

## Tester notes

The tester wrote no note.

## Coverage

A proxy saw each egress part.
answer:
I found one real defect and one minor one. The report is at `<project>/.nookku/tests/20261112-054518-b173/report.md`.

- **Business rule broken (turn 2):** the €80 refund was paid right away (`RF-81B206`). RULES.md:5 says any refund above €50 must wait for a manager to approve it. The cause is a unit mix-up at `app.py:60`: the code compares the amount in euros against `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000`, so the limit acts as €5000 instead of €50. state.json shows the refund recorded with no approval request.
- **Unsupported reply (turns 2–3):** the agent said the money should show up "in a few business days". Nothing in the tool results or the rules says that.
- The seal is intact, the audit shows no breaks, and there were no findings or tester notes. There's no app spec, so I didn't judge tone, boundaries, user goals or time limits. Turn 1 still took 61 seconds.
- A proxy saw every outside connection the app made.
